**Synopsis:**
The yen staged its strongest weekly gain since late July, driven by rising BOJ rate hike expectations ahead of its Sept 17–18 meeting, though it pulled back intraday on Friday. Broader FX markets are in a holding pattern ahead of US nonfarm payrolls and next week's CPI. Fed Governor Waller struck a relatively dovish tone, signaling a preference to hold rates steady if inflation continues to moderate — pulling September rate hike odds back to 50%. The dollar index is on track for a 0.7% weekly loss. JPMorgan flags risk of a sharp yen short squeeze toward 142–146. Geopolitical risk from US strikes on Iran is keeping crude elevated above $95/bbl, adding an inflation wildcard.
